name: ref_missing_is_empty_string
note: Unanswered and unknown fields are the empty string, never an error.

name: age_range_unanswered_null
note: Unanswered fails every relational comparison: an unanswered age is not in range.

name: eq_number_vs_string_is_numeric
note: If either side is a number, both are compared as numbers.

name: eq_unanswered_not_equal_zero
note: Unanswered is NaN as a number, so it equals no number, not even zero.

name: neq_unanswered_is_true_against_number
note: NaN != anything is true. A skip rule written with != shows the question when the field is unanswered.

name: not_string_zero_is_false
note: The string '0' is a non-empty string, so it is truthy. Only the number 0 is falsy.

name: mod_takes_sign_of_dividend
note: Truncated remainder like XPath and JavaScript, not Python's floored %.

name: arithmetic_with_unanswered_is_nan
note: NaN results are written as the string 'NaN' in this corpus.

name: div_by_zero_is_nan
note: XPath gives Infinity; we give NaN so no comparison on it can be true.

name: coalesce_keeps_zero
note: Zero is an answer, not an absence.

name: string_length_devanagari_counts_code_points
note: Code points, not grapheme clusters. JavaScript must count code points ([...s].length), not UTF-16 units.

name: regex_digit_class_is_ascii_only
note: \d is ASCII 0-9 only, as in JavaScript. Devanagari digits do not match.

name: concat_number_formats
note: Whole numbers print without a decimal point.

name: number_rejects_exponent
note: XPath numbers have no exponent, plus sign, hex, inf or nan.

name: today_defaults_to_kolkata
note: No timezone field means Asia/Kolkata. The same instant is 15 March in UTC.

name: today_in_utc_is_still_yesterday
note: Same instant as the case above, different date: the timezone is what decides today().

name: today_in_new_york_respects_dst
note: EDT is UTC-4 from 8 March 2026, so 03:00 UTC is 23:00 on the 15th.

name: early_morning_visit_today_passes_date_constraint
note: A 05:00 IST home visit: the visit date is today and must be accepted.

name: now_ignores_timezone
note: now() is always the UTC instant; only today() is local.

name: naive_datetime_string_is_refused_not_guessed
note: A datetime with no offset is NaN, so every comparison is false.

name: devanagari_digit_answer_is_not_a_number
note: A Hindi keyboard types these. Python's \d and float() would accept them; JavaScript does not, so both must say NaN.

name: number_trims_only_ascii_whitespace
note: A no-break space is not trimmed.

name: selected_no_break_space_is_not_a_separator
note: Only space, tab, CR and LF separate choices.

name: sum_decimals_plain_addition
note: Plain left-to-right addition, as a JavaScript loop does. Not math.fsum, which gives 0.6.

name: unary_minus_binds_tighter_than_plus
note: If unary minus bound looser than +, this would be -3.

name: boolean_vs_string_compares_as_booleans
note: A boolean on either side compares as booleans, and the non-empty string 'false' is true.

name: strings_equal_only_as_strings
note: Two strings never compare numerically.

name: chained_comparison_is_one_left_associative_level
note: Real XPath gives true (relational binds tighter than =). Here it is (3 = 3) > 2, and true as a number is 1. Deliberate; JavaScript must match this, not XPath.

name: unsupported_instance_lookup
note: Cascading-select lookups against a secondary instance are out of scope for Phase 1.

name: unsupported_bare_name
note: A bare name is an XPath path. Fields must be written ${age}.

name: unsupported_regex_computed_pattern
note: The pattern must be a literal so it can be checked at publish time.

name: unsupported_regex_named_group
note: Python-only syntax would diverge from JavaScript.

name: unsupported_devanagari_digit_literal
note: Digits in expressions are ASCII only.

name: unsupported_hindi_bare_name
note: A Hindi author writing a bare field name gets a clean refusal, not a crash.

name: to_string_1e16_is_exponent_form
note: Python repr, not JavaScript String(): the two diverge for |x| >= 1e16 and < 1e-4.

name: to_string_negative_1e16_is_exponent_form
note: Python repr, not JavaScript String(): the two diverge for |x| >= 1e16 and < 1e-4.

name: to_string_1e_minus_5_is_exponent_form
note: Python repr, not JavaScript String(): the two diverge for |x| >= 1e16 and < 1e-4.

name: to_string_1e_minus_4_stays_plain
note: The smallest magnitude that prints without an exponent.

name: to_string_largest_plain_integer
note: Whole numbers below 1e15 print as plain integers.

name: to_string_1e15_keeps_point_zero
note: PINS A PYTHON QUIRK: whole numbers from 1e15 up to 1e16 fall through to repr() and print with '.0', contrary to the docstring's 'no trailing .0'. JavaScript imitates it. If expr.py is fixed, change this case and the JS together.

name: to_string_16_digit_integer_keeps_point_zero
note: See to_string_1e15_keeps_point_zero.

name: to_string_overflow_is_infinity
note: A literal past the double range is Infinity in both languages; it prints as 'Infinity'.

name: regex_space_class_excludes_no_break_space
note: JavaScript's \s is Unicode; the server's re.ASCII \s is [ \t\n\r\f\v].

name: regex_space_class_excludes_line_separator
note: U+2028 is whitespace to JavaScript, not to Python ASCII.

name: regex_dot_matches_carriage_return
note: JavaScript's '.' refuses \r, U+2028 and U+2029; Python's refuses only \n.

name: regex_dollar_before_final_newline_does_not_extend_the_match
note: fullmatch needs the whole string, so 'a$' still cannot match 'a\n'.

name: regex_dollar_matches_before_final_newline
note: Python's $ matches before a trailing newline; JavaScript's does not.

name: regex_dot_is_one_code_point
note: Astral characters are one code point in Python; JavaScript without the u flag sees two UTF-16 units.

name: regex_start_and_end_of_string_anchors
note: \A and \Z are anchors in Python; plain JavaScript reads them as the letters A and Z.

name: regex_comma_first_quantifier
note: {,n} means {0,n} in Python; JavaScript reads it as literal text.

name: unsupported_regex_inline_flag
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_atomic_group
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_js_named_group
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_comment_group
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_bad_escape
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_backreference_without_group
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_repeat_bounds_reversed
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_bad_range_with_class
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_range_out_of_order
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_unterminated_set
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_unbalanced_open
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_unbalanced_close
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_nothing_to_repeat
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_multiple_repeat
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_quantified_anchor
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_quantified_word_boundary
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_incomplete_hex_escape
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_trailing_backslash
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_octal_out_of_range
note: Same rejection on both sides, at parse time.

name: unsupported_regex_escaped_paren_then_question_mark
note: SURPRISING BUT PINNED: the scan for '(?' flags does not see the backslash, so an optional escaped opening parenthesis is refused. Write '[(]?' instead.

name: string_length_astral_is_one
note: Code points, not UTF-16 units.

name: string_length_of_nan
note: NaN prints as 'NaN'.

name: negative_zero_in_sum
note: Python's sum starts from 0.0, so -0.0 + -0.0 is 0; JavaScript's loop must agree.

name: ref_allows_form_feed_inside_braces
note: Python's reference pattern uses \s (so \f and \v count) while its tokenizer's separators do not; both are reproduced.

name: unsupported_form_feed_between_tokens
note: Form feed is not a token separator, only inside ${ }.

name: limit_100_operands_is_accepted
note: The node limit is 200 parts: n operands joined by + use 2n-1 of them.

name: unsupported_101_operands_exceed_the_node_limit
note: 201 parts, one over MAX_NODES = 200.

name: limit_exactly_200_parts_is_accepted
note: One unary minus adds a part: 100 operands + 99 operators + 1 = 200.

name: unsupported_201_parts
note: 200 parts plus one more unary minus.

name: limit_49_nested_parentheses_is_accepted
note: MAX_DEPTH is 50 and the outermost expression is level 1, so 49 parentheses is the deepest that parses.

name: ref_named_constructor_is_unanswered
note: A JavaScript object has these members already; an unanswered field must still read as empty.

name: ref_named_proto_is_unanswered
note: A JavaScript object has these members already; an unanswered field must still read as empty.

name: ref_named_toString_is_unanswered
note: A JavaScript object has these members already; an unanswered field must still read as empty.

name: ref_named_hasOwnProperty_is_unanswered
note: A JavaScript object has these members already; an unanswered field must still read as empty.

name: ref_named_valueOf_is_unanswered
note: A JavaScript object has these members already; an unanswered field must still read as empty.

name: datetime_far_future_is_exact
note: Past the year 2255 the microsecond count exceeds 2**53; Python divides exactly, so JavaScript must too.

name: datetime_fraction_beyond_microseconds_is_truncated
note: Digits past the sixth are dropped, not rounded.

name: today_in_kiritimati_is_a_day_ahead
note: UTC+14.

name: today_in_etc_gmt_plus_12_is_a_day_behind
note: UTC-12 (the sign is inverted in Etc/ names).

name: count_counts_empty_rows_too
note: count() sees every row, empty or not; sum() skips the empty ones.
